title: Long-Term Hardship Hold Extensions and Recent Payment Arrangement Installments
content:
**Arrangements desk note — Hardship and Protective Holds.** The capacity cut of a long-term extension of a Long-Term Hardship Hold depends on the installments the consumer paid on payment plans dated less than three whole months before today, as shown by the paid-installment records of the consumer's Payment Arrangements. The cut is subtracted once from the days the long-term extension adds.

| Paid plan installments dated less than three whole months before today | Capacity cut |
|---|---|
| At least the steady-installment count of 3 | 30 calendar days (plan-steady days) |
| 1 or 2 | 15 calendar days (plan-some days) |
| None | Nothing |

**Whole months.** Whole months are the difference in calendar months between the installment's date and today, less one when today's day of the month is smaller than the date's day of the month; an installment counts only when that figure is less than three.

**Threshold, both sides.** Three paid installments in the period cut 30 days; two cut 15 days; none cut nothing.

**Example (hypothetical).** Today is 20 October. The consumer paid plan installments on 5 August, 5 September and 5 October. For 5 August the calendar months are 2 and today's day (20) is not smaller than 5, so the whole months are 2 — inside the period, like the other two. Three installments: the cut is 30 calendar days. Had the first installment been dated 21 July, its whole months would be 2 (3 calendar months, less one because 20 is smaller than 21), so it would also count.
